An institution's presence in a county does not confer jurisdiction over conduct elsewhere. Confirm incident site, legal entity, date and relevant authority; do not send to unrelated offices.

No personal addresses, individual clinician emails, private legal contact lists, message-board targeting or automatic dispatch. Coalition participation must be voluntary.
Private records, evidence, responses and receipt details belong in protected channels; only publish public/redacted material with authorization. No changes to status.md without actual dispatch.
This is not a complete list of all civil-rights practitioners, all affiliate sites, all deputy prosecutors, or 1,000 verified named individuals.

community-support.purpose: Reusable organizational support and referral knowledge; no recipient enrollment, endorsement or case-specific participation status.
constraints: A public organizational listing is not consent, verified deliverability, or authority to adjudicate a complaint.
Use only the stated purpose and limitations. Use only email routes explicitly published for the organization; URL-only records are not email destinations.
Community, spiritual and public policy channels receive only appropriate minimal or de-identified inquiries; never allegations about named people or private records.
A confidential intake label does not establish the security of a particular route; verify the official confidential procedure first.
Recheck jurisdiction, eligibility and current contact information before any real submission.

disease-disability-and-civic-resources.purpose: Public organizational resource directory for patient assistance, independent disability advocacy and general policy research/dialogue; separate from complaint dispatch.
usage_constraints: Use patient assistance or legal intake for the individual's care and access needs, only within the organization's scope and with confidentiality safeguards.

For general policy organizations and political parties, use de-identified systemic questions about patient safety, disability access, administrative review, and regulator accountability. Do not use this directory to distribute accusations against individual physicians or to mobilize pressure on their associates.

All six qualified California parties are included alphabetically without preference, ranking, endorsement or tailored political messaging. Civic/policy organizations reflect different public policy approaches; no political affiliation or opinion is inferred about individuals.
No private contact information, member lists, automated dispatch or claims of coalition participation. Advocacy programs have their own eligibility and priorities.

Where a source is an information or directory page, do not assume it accepts an individual complaint. The contact type distinguishes resource, general inquiry and policy channels. Emails and phone numbers are published organizational routes, not tested delivery; some have purpose limits.
Some organizations also appear in earlier files. Use stable organization identity to deduplicate; this file adds records rather than unique person counts.

news-media-resources.purpose: Directory of public newsroom pathways for independent, evidence-based public-interest reporting. Not a mailing list, allegation distribution mechanism or substitute for formal complaints.
editorial_use: Select outlets by geographic and editorial fit, not by number of recipients. Use one appropriate newsroom route; respect shared networks and avoid duplicative or repeated unsolicited messages.

A tip should distinguish firsthand observations, verifiable documentation, disputed allegations, inferences and the requested independent inquiry. Do not state unverified allegations as established findings.

Ask a newsroom about confidentiality before sharing sensitive personal or medical records. Ordinary email and most web forms are not encrypted; use the newsroom's own current confidential-submission guidance. Do not commit records or identities of confidential sources to the public repository.
Publication permission and confidentiality differ by outlet. Never assume off-the-record treatment unless agreed with the journalist. Some general contact pages are not dedicated tip routes.

No personal reporter contact harvest, unrelated contacts, automated dispatch, implied endorsement or reported acceptance. A press report does not file or extend any regulatory complaint or legal deadline.

victim-support-and-stanford-investigatio.purpose: Victim assistance and voluntary advocacy resources plus source-linked history of Stanford-related proceedings, independently of complaint dispatch.
constraints: No individual victim names or contact details collected. Use organization-level intake, consent-based support, and confidential evidence channels; support groups are not distribution lists.

Historical proceedings are not evidence of the truth of the current allegations. Distinguish Stanford University, Stanford Health Care, and pediatric institutions; distinguish regulators, plaintiffs/counsel, archives, reporting, and historical participants.

Only an appropriate agency with jurisdiction should receive specific allegations through established complaint channels. Historical-case-only records are evidence references, not outreach targets. No automatic dispatch or unrelated agencies contacted.

Where original survey reports or court dispositions are unavailable, record limits. For AHCJ entries, the source is an archive of CMS records; confirm official reports and correction plans through CDPH or CMS. No inference of continuing noncompliance from historic deficiencies.
Open status is as reported by source, not a current determination or finding. Public case information not exhaustive. No implied endorsement or coalition membership.

worker-rights-and-related-incident-repor.purpose: Source-backed historical reports of related institutional themes and public worker-rights, disability and policy resources in the Peninsula and Silicon Valley. Not a list of workers or associates to receive individual allegations.
scope_notes: Different legal entities and employment/education/healthcare jurisdictions are distinguished. Public reports do not establish a connected pattern, causation, or culpability in the user's case.

Preserve primary reporting, worker/union claims, organizational responses, formal dockets, contract outcomes and case dispositions as different evidence types. Open charges are allegations, not findings.

No private or public-facing personal survivor/worker contact details, names, lists of signatories, union member directories or communications channels collected. References identify the reporting organization or public docket. Group association does not establish shared experience.

Use competent medical/civil-rights authorities for individual allegations. Worker organizations and regional civic groups may supply relevant general policy or worker-rights resources through their public channels; membership and endorsements are not inferred.
No attempt to map Stanford's unrelated corporate, investor, alumni, family or personal influence network. Publicly documented employment and representation relationships are used for scope only.

Official CRONA site returned HTTP 406; representation verified from NLRB and public reporting. Other sources were reviewed as published; contact deliverability, current litigation dispositions and complete historical coverage are not guaranteed.
